column15: Lincoln County Process (charcoal mellowing through sugar-maple charcoal) is described by this source as removing impurities/corn taste rather than adding smoke, so I deliberately withheld a flavor.tsv 'smoky' row despite that being BRIEF.md's own worked example - my research contradicted it

Post-2018 core range vats in a small proportion of peated spirit (subtly smoky). Samples in this batch are all bare 'Jura' with no expression name, so no rule fires; Jura Prophecy (35ppm, heavily peated) added defensively in rule.tsv in case a future catalogue entry names it
Wikipedia does not explicitly state unpeated; inferred from its standard mainstream blended-Scotch profile with no peat/smoke mention anywhere in the article
No explicit peat statement found; inferred from its historic reputation as a deliberately light/mild style blend

Core range and main expressions are unpeated; a 'Nadurra Peated Cask' special edition exists but is not named in this batch's samples (Glenlivet, Glenlivet XXV, The Glenlivet, Glenlivet 1980's), so no rule added

This is the motivating example from BRIEF.md: unpeated, made about half the year; sibling Ledaig (this batch) is the heavily-peated malt made from the same stills the other half of the year. Owner Distell Group was itself acquired into Heineken N.V.

Heavily peated malt from Tobermory distillery (its original name). Not itself a brand string in this batch's input; added as a full row because BRIEF.md names Tobermory/Ledaig as the flagship sibling-pair example and Tobermory is in this batch

Westport=Glenmorangie is one of BRIEF.md's own named well-documented teaspooned exceptions. The cited URL confirms parent Glenmorangie's unpeated house style; two attempts to find a citation naming the Westport pseudonym itself specifically both returned 403. parentSlug=glenmorangie is NOT created in this batch's own producer.tsv - confirmed already present in out/04/producer.tsv (checked directly on disk)

Italian independent bottler based in Treviso, founded 1992 by Fabio Rossi (family import business since the 1920s/60s). Samples name Westport (=Glenmorangie, see that row), Caol Ila, Benrinnes, Bowmore, Glen Moray (all added as distillery/brand rows this batch) and 'Speybridge', which I could not confirm as a real distillery name (checked Speyside Distillery's Wikipedia page for an alt-name match, none found) - left unresolved, no row or alias created for it

~35-38ppm phenol, matching Lagavulin's figure (BRIEF.md's own 'heavy' example). Some sources call it 'medium' for its gentler mouthfeel despite the matching ppm - flagging the medium/heavy split for reviewer; per PROGRESS.md, other batches have already recorded this distillery both ways (02=heavy, 04=medium), so this is a third independent data point
~25ppm phenol, mid-range Islay peat. BRIEF.md itself names Bowmore as its own worked example of 'medium'
Wikipedia does not explicitly state unpeated; inferred from no peat/smoke mention and its role as a Diageo blending malt
Wikipedia does not explicitly state unpeated; inferred from no peat/smoke mention, standard Speyside profile

Independent Scotch blending house (whisky.com itself lists it under /independent-bottlers/), founded 2000 by John Glaser, based in Richmond, England (not Scotland). Bottles both unpeated (Hedonism, blended grain) and peated (Peat Monster, not in this batch's samples) ranges under many named lines with no single house peat level, hence unknown; see rule.tsv for a defensive Peat Monster rule. Owner left empty - independent company, no acquisition confirmed

Non-distilling independent blender of American whiskey and rum, Louisville KY, founded 2013; sources casks from multiple distilleries so has no single house peat level. Samples (Vantage, Dovetail, Seagrass, Batch 036, Foundation, Rye Batch 004) name no source distilleries, so no distillery rows added

Built around Lagavulin, with Caol Ila and Talisker also in the vatting, balanced by Speyside malt (Linkwood). Sources describe 'restrained smokiness' rather than a fully peated character despite the three peated malts, so recorded light rather than medium - flagging for reviewer given the pedigree of its component malts

Budget blended Scotch. Suspected (not confirmed) to be an Angus Dundee Distillers export line based on general trade familiarity; their own website (fetched this session) lists Tomintoul/Glencadam/Old Ballantruan but did not mention Highland Chief, so left unconfirmed rather than asserted. No citation obtained, peat left unknown

Believed to be Limestone Branch Distillery / Lux Row Distillers, Bardstown KY, per general trade knowledge; three separate fetch attempts to confirm this failed (404), so left uncited and owner empty rather than asserted; peat unknown per BRIEF.md's no-citation rule

Wikipedia does not explicitly state unpeated; inferred, no peat/smoke mention. This batch's catalogue brand string is 'Dufftown Distillery' (aliased here); the actual product line in every sample is 'The Singleton of Dufftown' (see singleton-of-dufftown, this batch)

Diageo's Dufftown-distillery expression of its 3-distillery 'Singleton' export brand (the others are Glendullan and Glen Ord, not in this batch) - deliberately did NOT add a bare 'Singleton' alias since that word is ambiguous across all three
Brand sold by Irish Distillers/Pernod Ricard to Sazerac in 2016; production continues under contract at Midleton. No explicit peat statement found; inferred from standard Irish blend convention

Makes both the unpeated Tyrconnell range (this batch) and the peated Connemara range (not in this batch), so has no single house peat level - left unknown deliberately, matching the Chichibu precedent set in batch 01
Unpeated single malt range from Cooley, explicitly distinguished by Wikipedia from Cooley's peated Connemara brand

Organic distillery at Drimnin on the Morvern peninsula (mainland Highland, opposite Mull); founded by Annabel Thomas, independent - owner left empty. Catalogue brand string 'Nc Nean' (no apostrophe) aliased here
Barton 1792 Distillery, Bardstown KY; standard bourbon mashbill, no peat mentioned anywhere

Unaged corn whiskey in Heaven Hill's portfolio alongside Mellow Corn; no peat tradition in American corn whiskey. defaultTypeName left empty - corn whiskey has no clean match in the closed type list (same call as batch-01's Sierra Norte)
No explicit peat statement found; inferred from standard Irish blend convention
No explicit peat statement; Canadian whisky has no peat tradition. defaultTypeName left empty - Canadian whisky has no clean match in the closed type list (same call as batch-01's Black Velvet)
Wikipedia does not explicitly state unpeated; inferred, no peat/smoke mention, mainly a Ballantine's blending malt

Craft distillery, Nashville TN (also historically Bowling Green KY); very experimental range. Could NOT confirm whether 'Triple Smoke' (named in this batch's samples) uses any peated malt among its smoke woods - some public descriptions pair cherry/beechwood/peat - so left unknown rather than guessing. Catalogue brand string is misspelled 'Corsaire' in this batch's input
Bourbon (Shelbyville/Lebanon KY) and rye (Lawrenceburg IN) come from two different mashbills/sites, so defaultTypeName left empty. No peat/smoke mentioned

Ukrainian craft producer; samples describe short-aged/unaged distillates finished on oak chips ('Білий Distillate', 'Aged on Bourbon/American Oak Chips'), unclear this is conventional grain whisky rather than a young craft spirit. No citation found this session, no web search budget spent (long tail)
Faux-Scottish-sounding name (Journey/Diamond/Elegance/Triple Wood range); could not confirm true country of origin or producer this session, left blank rather than assumed Scottish
One of a cluster of Japanese-styled budget brands in this batch (with Fujimi, Reki, Shin); no Wikipedia coverage found (fetch 404'd). Could not verify true origin/producer or peat status this session
Sample 'Fujimi Matsui Distillery' suggests a possible tie to Matsui Shuzo (Japan, Kurayoshi/Tottori) but this is unconfirmed; part of the same unresolved cluster as Shinobu/Reki/Shin
Part of the unresolved Japanese-styled budget cluster (see Shinobu); single product, no web presence found this session
Part of the unresolved Japanese-styled budget cluster (see Shinobu); single product, no web presence found this session
Product names explicitly say 'Канадіан' (Canadian), the basis for countryCode=CA; no other information found this session
Samples ('Ruediger', 'Oloroso Sherry Cask') read as a German-market brand but this is unconfirmed; two fetch attempts this session failed (403/404)
Heavy-metal-themed novelty brand ('Berry Metal', 'Field of Blood'); no information found this session, not searched (long tail budget)

Product names repeat French-Revolution imagery ('1789', 'No.7 1789'), the basis for countryCode=FR; 'Daucourt' (in one sample) is confirmed on Wikipedia to be only a French surname, not a spirits company, so that lead was dropped rather than guessed at
Named after the Irish folk ballad (confirmed on Wikipedia, which covers only the song, not a whiskey brand); assumed Irish whiskey from the name but the brand/producer itself is unconfirmed
No information found this session; likely an own-label/budget blend, not searched (long tail budget)
No information found this session; samples are 'Back to Black' / 'The Story of Back to Black' - own-label, origin unclear, not searched (long tail budget)

Single product, no information found this session; 'Bercloux' is a commune name in Charente-Maritime, France, but not confirmed as this brand's actual origin so countryCode left empty rather than guessed
Product name explicitly says 'Tennessee Straight', the basis for countryCode=US/defaultTypeName=tennessee; producer/distillery not identified this session
Single product, no information found this session; generic surname brand, too ambiguous to guess anything further

Likely NOT whisky - 'marc de Champagne' is a French grape-pomace brandy (eau-de-vie) from the Champagne region, almost certainly miscategorised in this catalogue; flagging for reviewer rather than inventing a whisky producer for it
Single product, no information found this session, not searched (long tail budget)
Product name explicitly says 'American Blend', the basis for countryCode=US/defaultTypeName=blend; producer not identified this session
